# A test calls a method of an instance and calls a method on what it answers,
# `c.g.loud().length()`. Through the provider, android handed the instance to
# the method as its first argument, beside the context it does take, and the
# test file did not compile.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

context #suffix("!")

component grid ui.node {
    var cells = ["a", "b"]

    func loud() => cells.map(func(s string) => s + suffix)

    ui.text(value=cells[0])
}

// The provider makes grid's method one a test calls through the instance.
component host ui.node {
    suffix("?") {
        grid #g()
    }
}

func testAMethodsAnswerIsAReceiver(t test.Test, c host) {
    t.assert(c.g.loud().length() == 2)
    t.assert(c.g.loud().map(func(s string) => string.length(s)).join(",") == "2,2")
}
